q6.answer: The fire step selects due schedules with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so only one worker holds the schedule row and the other skips it. next_fire_at is advanced in the same transaction, and UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING backs it up.

q7.answer: It is kept in job_schedules.next_fire_at. The fire step advances it to the first fire time after now() in the same transaction as run creation. It is also recomputed on re-enable, tenant resume, and cron or timezone edits, and set to NULL on disable.

q8.answer: The worker selects one queued run with next_attempt_at <= now() using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, re-checks status='queued' under the lock, then in the same transaction sets status='running', increments attempts_used, sets heartbeat_at and inserts the job_attempts row. Other workers skip the locked row, and afterwards it is no longer queued.

q9.answer: It is kept in job_runs.heartbeat_at, which the worker updates every 30 seconds while status='running'. The reaper step, run by any worker, finds running runs whose heartbeat_at is older than 2 minutes by database now() and treats them as dead.

q10.answer: The wait is recorded on the run itself: status goes back to 'queued' and next_attempt_at is set to now() plus 1 minute after attempt 1 or 5 minutes after attempt 2. The retry starts when any worker's normal claim step sees next_attempt_at <= now() and claims it like any queued run.

q11.answer: One job_runs row is recorded per fire time, enforced by UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time), and it holds the final status. One job_attempts row is recorded per execution try, with the worker, start and end times, outcome and error, enforced by UNIQUE (run_id, attempt_no).

q12.answer: attempts_used on job_runs is the fencing token. The stale worker's finishing update has WHERE status='running' AND attempts_used = its own attempt number, and the takeover's claim has incremented it, so the update matches zero rows. The stale worker then rolls back and writes nothing. Its attempt row update also fails because the reaper already marked it abandoned.
